gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named tester measured a Victron SmartShunt 500A against a Fluke and a bench meter: it read 2–5% low at 1–10 A and drew about 4 mA on standby, against the less than 1 mA in Victron's datasheet that cartvoltage quotes.
standout_why: I compared against cartvoltage.com/best-lithium-battery-meter-golf-cart (cited, 2026-10-29) and cartvoltage.com/golf-cart-battery-meter-wrong-lithium (2026-10-12/29). The first gives only maker figures: Renogy ±1% from its product page, Victron standby under 1 mA from its datasheet, and Junctek 0.4 W module and 0.5 W display from its manual. It says no independent tester or lab measured anything. The second gives a resting-voltage SOC table with no named source and no accuracy figure for any meter. The other results are maker and retailer battery pages, with no measurement of any meter. So nothing ChatGPT got contains a named measurement. The best one I found comes from a single unit tested by one forum user, which is why this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: This supports the Victron SmartShunt as the app pick, but with two caveats a golf cart owner needs. First, its standby draw measured about 4 mA, roughly four times the datasheet figure. Over a 90-day winter layup that is about 8.6 Ah, or about 8% of a 105 Ah pack, so a cart left in storage should be switched off or disconnected. Second, Footprint Hero measured its Bluetooth range dropping from 90–100 ft in the open to 30 ft inside an enclosed battery compartment. A shunt under a cart seat is reliable for reading from the driver's seat, not from the house. No named tester has measured the Renogy 500A or the Junctek KG140F, so this does not overturn the Renogy pick for a dash screen. It only means the Renogy's ±1% is unverified, while the Victron at least has a named bench check.

findings.label: Low-current reading error vs reference meters
findings.source_title: Mismatch Smartshunt 500A and specifications – Victron Community
findings.note: Measured by user 'mystudio', posted 2025-12-12. The reference was a Fluke plus a bench DMM, which agreed with each other, on a known current source. My arithmetic: (4.89−5.002)/5.002 = −2.2%, (9.80−10.002)/10.002 = −2.0%. One unit only. User Ulfilas (2025-12-15) replied that Victron's ±0.4% is full scale, about ±2 A on a 500 A shunt.

findings.label: Standby (self-consumption) current, measured
findings.source_title: Mismatch Smartshunt 500A and specifications (page 2) – Victron Community
findings.note: Measured by 'mystudio' with a desktop DMM, posted 2025-12-19. The first post (2025-12-12) said 'above 3 mA'. cartvoltage quotes the datasheet as under 1 mA. My arithmetic: 4 mA × 24 h × 90 days = 8.64 Ah, about 8% of a 105 Ah 48 V pack over a 90-day layup. The thread does not give the bank voltage.

findings.label: Amp-hour count on a full capacity test, before and after user shunt trim
findings.value: 324–325 Ah read vs 330 Ah expected (about 1.5–1.8% low); shunt resistance about 2.4% low; within spec to about 150 A after trimming
findings.source_title: Mismatch Smartshunt 500A and specifications (page 2) – Victron Community
findings.note: Posted by 'mystudio' 2025-12-22 (capacity test) and 2026-01-18 (after trimming the shunt to 0.1 mΩ; the user notes this likely voids the warranty). Victron staff member Thiemo van Engelen only asked for the serial number (HQ2308VJVQA). This is one unit and not a lab result.
